subject: Multivariate LCM varying starting dates  for sime participants in a cohort.

messages.author: 85cbee01ee30ad74
messages.subject: Multivariate LCM varying starting dates  for sime participants in a cohort.
parts:
Hi all,

I am planning to run a multivariate latent curve model. I want to describe the relationship between some  variables  and some outcomes across  4 time points (in months). The issue is that some of the participants  starting date in the cohort vary , (e.g., at time point 1, participant 1 started  on 10/2/23 participant 2 started on 17/2/23, that happening just at the inclusion in the cohort).

How can I deal with this issue in terms of modeling in Lavaan?
 I would really appreciate any advice or suggestion!

Thanks,
Dan

messages.author: f6d12b388faad456
messages.subject: Re: Multivariate LCM varying starting dates for sime participants in a cohort.
parts:
Hi, Dan,

From what I understand, the model would consist of 4x latent factors (x = number of factors you are measuring at each time point; 4x because each one will be measured 4 times). In this case, "date" would be ordinal and assessed by the latent factors (factor 1.1 is the factor 1 at date 1, factor 1.2 is factor 1 at date 2).
If you want to add the exact date as a covariate, I'm not aware of a way to do that. Maybe you could define the starting date of participant 1 as 0 and the remaining observations are equal to how many days have passed since participant 1 started, but I think this would make the interpretation of date meaningless.

Best,
Yago

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Multivariate LCM varying starting dates for sime participants in a cohort.
parts:
Dan,
I am not sure that I understand the details of your data, particularly after reading Yago's reply.  Is it only the first time point that varies?  If so, do the intervals between time points stay fixed with all the time points varying together, or does the first interval vary depending on the date? Are there only two cohorts or more?

It is hard to offer any concrete advice without a clearer understanding.  However, my initial thoughts are these.  If the differences are very small in relation to the size of the time intervals, the differences might be ignorable.  If not, but the intervals are the same size for all participants and you expect a simple additive effect, then a time-invariant covariate might suffice.  If the impact is more complicated than that and the start patterns are not too many relative to the sample size, then the best option might be a multiple group analysis with a separate group for each start pattern.

Keith
